lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Christian Bauer is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Christian Bauer is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Christian kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Christian's gone." Jorge looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Christian." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Vera blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Ritual & Meaning (Level 1). Marking the dead matters. Even without religion, ritual holds grief.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Christian Bauer, 41 days. The mantle passes to Vera Beck.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Vera Beck, 42 — a tattoo artist. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Scream Cheese.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Christian — and Christian is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: You knew Christian — not the office, the person. The fire keeps expecting them, and so do you. That's a heavier kind of stepping up. (+5 trauma)
d41: At the grave, Dmitri, Aria, Ethan and 3 more speak for Vera — "Christian trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Vera before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
